evidence: Cic. Lael. 90: cujus aurēs clausae vēritātī sunt (Lewis & Short s.v. salūs)
terms.comment: Cicero’s words, said by him of ears shut to the truth; of ears blocked by the pressure in an aeroplane the use is ours. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for that; to stop one’s ears is aurēs obtūrāre (Hor. Ep. 2.2.105, in Lewis & Short; M-O s.v. actions: stop up one’s ears).

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Lewis & Short: salus · Lewis & Short: obturo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. actions: stop up one’s ears.
